pages.name: Round once
pages.text: Roll a circle once and its rim lays down its [[circumference]]. For every circle it is just over 3 diameters, a number called [[π]], about 3.14. So C = πd.

pages.name: Round a pipe
pages.task: A pipe is 10 cm across. How far is it round?
pages.why: Across is the diameter, so d = 10 cm. The way round is C = πd = π × 10 = 31.42 cm, just over 3 times across.

pages.alt: A pipe's end, a circle 10 centimetres across, standing on the ground. It rolls once and its rim lays down a track 31.42 centimetres long, pi times 10 centimetres.

pages.name: Wedges into a rectangle
pages.text: Cut a circle into wedges and lay them top to tail. They make a rough rectangle πr long, half of the way round, 2πr, and one [[radius]] tall. So the area is πr × r = πr².

pages.name: Grow the radius
pages.text: Drag the radius. The circle covers just over 3 of the 4 squares on its radius, π of them, each r × r. So twice the radius makes four times the area.

The radius is 2 centimetres; the square on it holds 4 of those 1 centimetre squares, and the circle covers 12.57 square centimetres, pi times the square on its radius. That is 4 times the area at a radius of 1 centimetre, 3.14 square centimetres.

pages.name: Halve it first
pages.task: This solid round wire is 2 mm across. What is its [[cross-section]]?
pages.why: Halve the diameter first, so r = 1 mm. The cross-section is πr² = π × 1² = 3.14 mm².

pages.name: Twice as wide
pages.task: Solid round wire B is twice as wide across as wire A. How many times A's cross-section does it have?
pages.why: B's radius is twice A's, and the radius is squared. The square on B's radius holds 2 × 2 = 4 of A's squares, so B has 4 times the cross-section, 12.57 mm² against 3.14 mm².

pages.name: A ring
pages.text: A pipe's end is a ring, an [[annulus]]. Its area is the whole circle less the hole. Work out each with πr², then take one from the other.

pages.name: The metal in a pipe
pages.task: A pipe is 12 cm across outside and 10 cm across inside. What is the area of its metal ring?
pages.why: Halve both, so the radii are 6 cm and 5 cm. The whole circle is π × 6² = 113.10 cm² and the hole is π × 5² = 78.54 cm², so the ring is 34.56 cm².
pages.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 222" width="340" style="fill:rgb(29, 31, 34);stroke:none;stroke-width:1px;font-family:system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;font-size:16px;font-weight:400;text-anchor:start" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" height="222"><g><path d="M30 122a60 60 0 1 0 120 0a60 60 0 1 0 -120 0ZM40 122a50 50 0 1 0 100 0a50 50 0 1 0 -100 0Z" fill-rule="evenodd" style="fill:rgb(214, 224, 235);stroke:rgb(29, 31, 34);stroke-width:2px"/><g><circle cx="250" cy="122" r="50" style="fill:rgb(207, 232, 228);stroke:rgb(29, 31, 34);stroke-width:2px"/><line x1="250" y1="122" x2="300" y2="122" style="stroke:rgb(29, 31, 34);stroke-width:2.25px;stroke-linecap:round"/><circle cx="250" cy="122" r="3"/><text x="275" y="115" text-anchor="middle" style="stroke:rgb(255, 255, 255);stroke-width:3.25px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:middle;paint-order:stroke">5 cm</text></g><g><line x1="90" y1="122" x2="30" y2="122" style="stroke:rgb(29, 31, 34);stroke-width:2.25px;stroke-linecap:round"/><circle cx="90" cy="122" r="3"/><text x="68" y="115" text-anchor="middle" style="stroke:rgb(255, 255, 255);stroke-width:3.25px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:middle;paint-order:stroke">6 cm</text></g><g><text x="338" y="15" text-anchor="end" style="fill:rgb(11, 106, 112);stroke:rgb(255, 255, 255);stroke-width:3.25px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:end;paint-order:stroke">the metal ring</text><text x="338" y="38" text-anchor="end" style="stroke:rgb(255, 255, 255);stroke-width:5px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:20px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:end;paint-order:stroke">113.10 − 78.54 = 34.56 cm²</text></g></g><g/></svg>
pages.alt: A pipe's end, a ring 12 centimetres across outside and 10 centimetres across inside. Halved, the radii are 6 and 5 centimetres. The hole, a circle of its own, is lifted out, and the ring is 113.10 minus 78.54, which is 34.56 square centimetres.

pages.name: Back to the width
pages.task: A round shaft's end has an area of 28.27 cm². How wide across is it?
pages.why: Undo each step. 28.27 ÷ π = 9.00, which is r², so r = √9 = 3 cm. Across is 2 × 3 = 6 cm.

pages.name: Round the drum
pages.task: A cable drum's barrel has a radius of 30 cm. How far is it once round the barrel?
pages.why: With the radius, C = 2πr = 2 × π × 30 = 188.50 cm. That is the same as πd with d = 60 cm.
pages.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 210" width="340" style="fill:rgb(29, 31, 34);stroke:none;stroke-width:1px;font-family:system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;font-size:16px;font-weight:400;text-anchor:start" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" height="210"><g><line x1="8" y1="200" x2="332" y2="200" style="stroke:rgb(169, 175, 182);stroke-width:1.5px"/><line x1="46" y1="200" x2="284.76" y2="200" style="stroke:rgb(29, 31, 34);stroke-width:3px;stroke-linecap:round"/><circle cx="284.76" cy="162" r="38" style="fill:none;stroke:rgb(29, 31, 34);stroke-width:3px"/><circle cx="284.76" cy="200" r="4.5"/><g><text x="338" y="15" text-anchor="end" style="fill:rgb(11, 106, 112);stroke:rgb(255, 255, 255);stroke-width:3.25px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:end;paint-order:stroke">once round</text><text x="338" y="38" text-anchor="end" style="stroke:rgb(255, 255, 255);stroke-width:5px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:20px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:end;paint-order:stroke">2 × π × 30 = 188.50 cm</text></g></g><g/></svg>
pages.alt: A cable drum's barrel, a circle of radius 30 centimetres, standing on the ground. It rolls once and its rim lays down a track 188.50 centimetres long, pi times 60 centimetres.

pages.name: One or two
pages.task: Which has more cross-section, one solid wire 4 mm across or two solid wires 2 mm across?
pages.why: Twice the width makes four times the area. One 4 mm wire has 12.57 mm², and two 2 mm wires have 2 × 3.14 = 6.28 mm², half as much.

pages.name: A round hatch
pages.task: A round hatch cover is 0.6 m across. What is its area?
pages.why: Halve the diameter, so r = 0.3 m. Then πr² = π × 0.3² = π × 0.09 = 0.28 m².
